scenes.headline: How a Transformer turns tokens into the next token
scenes.sub: Attention, the residual stream, the MLP, and the KV cache
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sterling! Nearly every language model descends from this one block, stacked. Here's how it works.

scenes.text: Each token carries one vector, its residual stream. Every block adds to it twice: attention reads earlier tokens, then an MLP transforms each token alone.
scenes.say: Each token carries one vector. Every block adds to it twice: attention reads earlier tokens, then an MLP works on each token alone.

scenes.title: One block, drawn as a stream

steps.say: Each token id picks a row of an embedding table. That vector starts its residual stream.
Attention reads a normalised copy, gathers from earlier tokens, and adds back.

steps.note: each token alone, four times wider
steps.say: The MLP does the same per token: normalise, widen four times, narrow, add.
After the last block, one matrix scores every token in the vocabulary.

parts.note: every query dotted with every key
parts.say: Every query meets every key: one score per pair.

parts.note: d_k = 64: scores spread 8 times wider, so divide by 8
parts.say: Divide by the root of the head width. Otherwise the scores spread, and softmax goes one-hot.

parts.note: each row becomes weights that sum to one
parts.say: Softmax makes each row sum to one, and those weights average the values.

steps.label: No mask: every token sees every token
steps.say: Unmasked, every token could read its own answer.

steps.label: Causal: only keys at or before the query
steps.note: future scores set to minus infinity
steps.say: So future scores become minus infinity. Each token sees only its past, and one pass trains every position.
Stack the block. Llama 2 seven B has thirty-two, all writing to one stream.

steps.note: per block: MLP 135.3 million weights, attention 67.1 million
steps.say: Per block, the MLP holds two thirds of the weights.

steps.note: earlier keys and values never change
steps.say: Generating, earlier keys and values never change, so each layer caches them.

scenes.label: numbers cached per token in Llama 2 7B
scenes.note: 512 KiB per token at 16-bit; 2 GiB for 4,096 tokens
scenes.say: That's over a quarter of a million numbers per token. A full context needs over two billion bytes.

scenes.text: Attention moves information between tokens, the MLP transforms each token alone, and the residual stream carries both up the stack.
scenes.say: Attention moves information between tokens, the MLP transforms each one, and the stream carries both.

recap: Attention: scaled dot products, masked to the past
Residual stream: every sublayer adds, none overwrites
KV cache: earlier keys and values, kept
scenes.say: Attention, masked to the past. A stream every sublayer adds to. A cache for the past.
